Dr C Podges Incorporated trades as CP Dental and Aesthetics, a family dental practice built around preventive care. Twice-yearly check-ups and cleanings are used to catch cavities, gum disease and orthodontic issues early, and the practice's range runs from basic restorative work and paediatric dentistry to endodontic treatment, removable and fixed prosthodontics, and cosmetic dentistry.

Alongside general dentistry, the practice also offers aesthetic treatments including anti-wrinkle injections, giving patients a single destination for both oral health and facial aesthetics. It is based on Sluysken Street in Welgemoed, treating patients from across the Bellville and Tyger Valley area. Patients looking for a dentist who treats the whole family, from first fillings to cosmetic work, will find a practical, health-first approach here.

Dr Carl Ensil Table View Dental Studio Inc is a general dentistry practice that also provides emergency dental care, from its premises on Blaauwberg Road in Table View. The team handles routine consultations, fillings, crown work and root canal treatment, along with implants and orthodontic braces for patients wanting straighter teeth.

Patients, including children and those who find dental visits stressful, have been treated with particular care to keep them calm and comfortable through procedures. The practice is set up to see both scheduled check-ups and dental emergencies as they arise. It is a convenient option for families in Table View needing a dentist who can also fit in urgent appointments outside a routine booking.

Dr RB Daya runs a general medical practice on Welgelegen Avenue in Strandfontein, offering day-to-day consultations for illness, injury and ongoing health concerns. As a dispensing practice, prescribed medication can be collected on site straight after a consultation rather than at a separate pharmacy, which saves patients an extra stop.

The practice is contracted to a wide range of medical aid schemes, so members can usually be seen and have their visit claimed without paying the full fee upfront. Consultations are conducted in English. It serves the Strandfontein community and the surrounding Cape Flats suburbs, with a working week that includes a shorter Wednesday and Saturday morning hours for patients who cannot get in during the week.

Eagle Lighting Somerset West is one of several Cape Town branches of the Eagle Lighting chain, alongside stores in Tygervalley, Lakeside, Maitland and the Cape Town city centre. The showroom stocks a broad range of light fittings, bulbs and electrical accessories for homes and businesses, covering everyday fixtures through to decorative and outdoor lighting.

Customers have noted knowledgeable staff able to advise on fixing or replacing a fitting, though some specialised ranges are better stocked than others and certain items may need to be ordered in. The branch trades from the Somerset Decor Centre on Jigger Avenue in Somerset West. It suits homeowners and renovators shopping locally for lighting rather than ordering online.

Eastlake Barber Shop is a men's barbering business operating from Shop 13 in the Eastlake Shopping Centre in Marina Da Gama. The core service is the classic men's haircut, backed up by beard trims, head shaves and a traditional hot towel shave for customers wanting the fuller barbershop treatment rather than a quick trim.

Being inside a small suburban shopping centre makes it an easy stop alongside other errands, with walk-ins generally welcome rather than requiring a long lead time to book. The shop keeps long daily hours, with a shorter day on Sundays, making it workable for both weekday regulars and weekend visits. It is a straightforward option for men in the Marina Da Gama and Muizenberg area looking for a proper barbershop rather than a salon.

Ecco Il Caffè is a coffee shop operating from the Devil's Peak Brewery premises on Durham Avenue in Salt River. The menu runs through breakfast plates, bagels, burgers and casual lunches, built around the café's own house coffee blend rather than a supplied commercial roast.

Being based at a working brewery gives the space an industrial, laid-back feel that has made it a regular stop for students and workers from the surrounding Salt River and Woodstock area, alongside brewery visitors popping in before or after a tasting. It functions as a daytime café first, serving coffee and food rather than operating as a bar. Expect a casual setting suited to a quick breakfast or a working lunch rather than a sit-down dinner.

Eerste River Paint & Hardware is a neighbourhood hardware and paint shop on Bobs Way in Eerste River. It stocks the everyday range a hardware store needs to carry: building materials, hand tools, fixings and a paint selection for touch-ups and full repaints, aimed at local households and small building jobs rather than bulk trade supply.

As a standalone, locally run store rather than a branch of a national chain, it serves as a practical first stop for residents needing supplies without a long drive to a bigger retailer. It trades from Bobs Way, within reach of the surrounding Eerste River and Kleinvlei communities. Weekend trading, including Saturdays, makes it a convenient option for DIY and maintenance jobs done outside the working week.

Ellies Electronics in Ndabeni is the Cape Town branch of Ellies, a South African manufacturer, importer and distributor of lighting and electrical products that has been operating since 1979. The range runs from LED lighting, including floodlights and general household and commercial fittings, through to surge protection products designed to guard televisions, appliances and office equipment against power spikes.

Operating as part of a long-running national supplier rather than a single independent shop gives the branch access to a wide catalogue and backed warranties on items such as its high-surge electrical products. The branch is based on Morningside Road in Ndabeni, serving trade customers and households across greater Cape Town. It is a useful stop for anyone needing lighting or surge-protection equipment backed by an established manufacturer rather than an unbranded import.

Empire Cafe is a breakfast and lunch spot on York Road in Muizenberg, set inside a converted vintage building that gives the space more character than a standard strip-mall café. The kitchen runs an ever-changing menu rather than a fixed printed one, so regulars can expect some variation between visits instead of ordering the same dish every time.

Coffee is a particular focus, with the café serving organic beans rather than a mainstream commercial blend. Seating on the balcony takes in sea views, which has made it a popular stop for both locals and visitors exploring the Muizenberg area. The café is open daily and is well suited to a relaxed breakfast or lunch before or after time spent on the nearby beach.

Excellent Meat Market is a family-owned Halaal butchery that has traded from the corner of Epping Avenue and Halt Road in Elsies River since 1970. Alongside this branch, the business runs sister stores in Athlone and Wetton, giving it the buying scale of a small chain while each shop still runs as a neighbourhood butchery.

The counter sells fresh Halaal beef, lamb, poultry and prepared cuts, with online ordering also available through the group's website for customers who would rather collect or arrange delivery than queue in-store. Trading from Elsies River for more than five decades, it has built a loyal local following in the area. It is a solid choice for Halaal meat bought fresh rather than pre-packaged, with trade running into the weekend as well as on weekdays.

Excellent Meat Market's Ottery branch, on Wetton Road, is part of a Halaal butchery group that has been trading since 1970 and also runs stores in Elsies River and Athlone. The shop sells fresh beef, lamb and poultry over the counter, cut to order rather than pre-packaged, along with the processed and prepared lines typical of a dedicated butchery.

Customers can also order through the group's online shop for collection or delivery, an option alongside the usual walk-in counter service. Having been established for more than fifty years, the Ottery store has built a steady base of regulars who return for its meat quality rather than shopping on price alone. It trades six days a week, including Saturdays and Sunday mornings, fitting around a normal working week.

Fabric Friends is a fabric and haberdashery shop at Ramir Court in Boston, Bellville, stocking a wide range of dress and craft material alongside ribbons, buttons, zips and other sewing trimmings. Regular customers describe it as a reliable source for items that smaller general stores don't carry, including hard-to-find haberdashery pieces and large fabric offcuts sold at a lower price than buying off the roll.

Stock is said to change regularly, so visitors who don't find a particular fabric on one trip may find something suitable on a later visit. The shop has built a loyal following among sewers and crafters in Bellville and the wider Northern Suburbs over a long period of trading. It is open through the week and on Saturday mornings, closed on Sundays, and remains a reliable stop for anyone who sews regularly.

Fish Hoek Fisheries is a fish and chips takeaway on Main Road in Fish Hoek, frying to order rather than holding pre-cooked stock on a warmer. The menu centres on hake and other fresh fish, calamari and prawns, served with chips in the traditional South African takeaway style.

Being a long-standing fixture on Fish Hoek's main strip rather than a newly opened outlet, it has built a following among locals who treat it as a regular dinner option rather than an occasional treat. Trade follows an unusual weekly pattern, open Tuesday to Thursday and on Saturdays, closed on Fridays, Sundays and Mondays, so regulars generally plan around those specific days. It suits anyone after a straightforward takeaway meal rather than a sit-down seafood dinner in the Fish Hoek valley.

Fisherman's Lane is a fish and chips takeaway inside Capricorn Square shopping centre in Muizenberg, trading alongside the centre's supermarket, banks and other retail stores. Fish is fried to order rather than kept under a heat lamp, and the menu extends to Gatsbys and grilled seafood seasoned with the brand's own spice blend.

Being based inside an established shopping centre means parking and other errands are close at hand, which suits a quick takeaway stop rather than a destination seafood outing. It serves shoppers and residents across Muizenberg and the surrounding Prince George Drive corridor. Trading hours run into the evening on weekdays and weekends, with the store closed on Sundays, making it a convenient weekday or Saturday night takeaway option.

Formula 1 Fitment Centre is a tyre and fitment workshop on Koeberg Road in Brooklyn, covering the core jobs a fitment centre handles: tyre sales and fitting, wheel alignment and balancing, and mag wheel sales for drivers wanting a style change as well as a replacement set. Beyond tyres, the workshop also fits shock absorbers, car batteries and exhaust systems.

Covering this wider range of mechanical fitment work alongside tyres means customers can often get more than one job done in a single visit rather than being sent elsewhere for suspension or exhaust work. The centre is categorised locally as both a tyre dealer and an automotive repair business, reflecting that broader scope. It serves motorists across Brooklyn and the neighbouring Paarden Eiland and Milnerton areas, trading through the week and on Saturdays.

Foxcroft is a restaurant and bakery in the High Constantia Centre, opened in October 2016 as a sister restaurant to a well-known fine-dining establishment elsewhere in Cape Town. The kitchen serves a considered lunch and dinner menu built around ingredients sourced from local farmers and international suppliers, alongside a separate bakery counter trading throughout the day.

The bakery runs on its own daily schedule from morning into the afternoon, independent of the restaurant's lunch and dinner service times, so visitors can pop in for fresh bread or pastries outside of meal hours. Based in Constantia, it draws diners from across the Southern Suburbs. It suits both a planned sit-down meal and a casual stop for baked goods on the way past.

Future Tool is a tool and hardware retailer operating from Viking Business Place in Thornton, selling a working range of hand and power tools, workshop equipment and related hardware. Customers can shop in person, order online for delivery, or choose curbside pickup instead of walking through the store, which suits tradespeople collecting an order on the way to a job.

Operating from an industrial business park rather than a high-street shopfront keeps the focus on stock and service for tool buyers rather than general retail foot traffic. It is based in Thornton, within easy reach of the surrounding Elsies River and Epping industrial areas. Trading hours run shorter on Fridays and the store is closed over weekends, which fits a trade-focused rather than weekend-shopper customer base.

Giant Hyper is a large food and household hypermarket in Epping that grew out of a Giant Sweets and Chocolates store first opened in the area in 2001. The store now runs as a full hypermarket, with dedicated butchery, bakery, deli, hot-food and diner sections alongside the main grocery and household aisles.

All products sold across its departments are strictly Halaal, and the business belongs to the Consumer Goods and Services Ombudsman, giving customers a formal route for complaints if something goes wrong. Trading from Benbow Avenue in Gunners Circle, it serves shoppers across Epping and the surrounding industrial and residential areas looking to do a full grocery run under one roof. Weekday, Friday and weekend hours are shorter than during the main trading day, so visitors should check timing before a late shop.

Goldfish Cafe & Eatery is a seafood-focused restaurant on Beach Road in Strand, serving breakfast, lunch and dinner with a menu built around fresh, sustainably sourced seafood. Italian coffee is served alongside the food menu, and the restaurant offers dine-in, takeaway and outdoor seating for customers who want to eat by the beachfront rather than inside.

The restaurant has been named a finalist in KFM's Best of the Cape awards in more than one year, reflecting a following that extends beyond its immediate neighbourhood. It trades from Beach Road in Strand, within the greater Strand and Helderberg coastal area. It is a solid option for a full seafood meal through the day rather than a quick snack, with outdoor seating making it workable for a relaxed weekend breakfast too.

Gringo's Cantina is a pub and pizzeria in Boston, Bellville, serving pizzas, burgers and Mexican-style pub food alongside a full bar. It operates across several categories at once, functioning as a restaurant, takeaway and neighbourhood pub depending on when customers visit.

Beyond food and drinks, the venue runs pool and darts competitions and holds regular karaoke nights, giving it more of a social, entertainment-led pub atmosphere than a straightforward dining room. It is based on 12th Avenue in Boston, serving the Bellville and wider Northern Suburbs crowd looking for a casual night out rather than a formal dinner. Later closing hours on Tuesdays, Fridays and Saturdays suit an after-work or weekend evening crowd, with Sunday trade finishing earlier in the day.

Happy Rooster is a Portuguese-style restaurant on the first floor of the Muizenberg Station building, serving trinchado steak and peri-peri chicken from a kitchen that opened in late 2025. Large windows take in views over the surrounding area, giving diners a reason to sit in rather than order straight to takeaway.

Despite being tucked above the railway station rather than facing the beach directly, reviewers have rated it worth the short walk across the tracks for the food and setting. The restaurant offers dine-in, takeaway and delivery, giving customers flexibility beyond a sit-down meal. It serves the Muizenberg community and visitors drawn to the area's growing café and restaurant scene, with an earlier opening on some days of the week.

Hawkes & Findlay is an old-fashioned hardware store in Observatory that has been trading since 1972, built around personalised service rather than a big-box self-service layout. Staff advise customers directly on paint, timber, roofing supplies, masonry materials, plumbing and gardening equipment, as well as general tools and hardware.

The range also runs to practical gift items alongside the core trade stock, giving it a slightly broader offering than a purely trade-focused supplier. Having traded from the same Observatory corner for more than fifty years, it has become a known fixture for residents in Observatory and the surrounding university area rather than a recent arrival. It is open through the week and Saturday mornings, closed on Sundays, suited to DIY jobs that need proper advice rather than just a product off a shelf.

HBC Systems manufactures and supplies equipment for the emergency services sector from its base in Epping Industria, with dual battery systems and solar panel setups among its core product lines. The business has supplied this specialised market for more than fifteen years, building equipment that emergency crews can depend on in the field.

Quality control is central to the business, since clients rely on the equipment to carry out their duties safely rather than treating it as general-purpose gear. HBC Systems operates as a manufacturer rather than a reseller, giving it closer control over how its battery and power systems are built. Based in the Bofors Industrial Park in Epping, it trades Monday to Friday, with shorter hours on Fridays and no weekend trading.

Highlands Primary School is a public primary school in Woodlands, Mitchells Plain, which opened in 1975 with just 23 learners enrolled. It has since grown substantially, now teaching more than 800 learners under a staff of roughly two dozen educators, making it a well-established part of the local school network rather than a smaller or newer campus.

As a public school, it follows the standard national curriculum and admissions process, drawing most of its intake from families living in Woodlands and the neighbouring Mitchells Plain suburbs. Over five decades of operation it has built a stable identity within the area's schooling landscape. Classes run on the usual public school day, from morning until early afternoon, Monday to Friday, in step with the rest of the Mitchells Plain school calendar.

Hugo The Hair Company is a hair salon in Panorama that has been trading since 2005, offering cuts, colour and balayage alongside anti-frizz treatments for clients wanting smoother, more manageable hair. The salon works with established professional brands including Goldwell, Kevin.Murphy and Paul Mitchell rather than generic in-house products.

Blow-dries and women's haircuts form the bulk of day-to-day bookings, with colour work and chemical treatments available for clients wanting a bigger change. Having traded from the same Panorama Road address for close to two decades, the salon has built a regular client base across Panorama and the surrounding Parow area rather than relying mainly on passing trade. It is closed on Mondays and Sundays, trading Tuesday to Saturday to suit a standard working week.

Hungry Lion Goodwood Mall is a branch of the Hungry Lion fast-food chain, which started as a single small eatery in Stellenbosch in 1997 and has since grown into a major fried-chicken brand with more than 500 stores across nine African countries. The Goodwood Mall outlet serves the chain's fried chicken, burgers and family meal buckets for dine-in or takeaway.

Being part of a large, established chain rather than an independent operator means consistent recipes and pricing across branches, while still relying on each store's own team to keep up with the mall's daily foot traffic. The outlet trades from inside Goodwood Mall in Goodwood, serving shoppers and the surrounding Goodwood Estate community. It stays open every day of the week into the evening, making it a straightforward stop before or after a shopping trip.

Jafmed Pharmacy is a family-owned pharmacy on Ottery Road in Ottery, dispensing both acute and chronic prescription medicine for patients across the area. Beyond dispensing, the pharmacy runs its own in-house screening services, including blood pressure, cholesterol and blood sugar testing, and administers vitamin and other simple injections.

Being contracted to all major medical aid schemes means most chronic medicine claims can be processed directly rather than requiring patients to pay upfront and claim back later. A delivery service is also available for patients who cannot collect their prescriptions in person. The pharmacy serves the Ottery community and surrounding suburbs, trading long hours into the evening on weekdays and Saturdays, with Sundays closed, so prescriptions can be collected outside normal working hours too.

Jarryds is a Parisian-inspired brunch bistro and vinyl lounge on Regent Road in Sea Point, serving breakfast, salads, burgers and bagels through the day rather than running a separate dinner service. Coffee and latte art are a visible part of the experience, with the venue's own baristas building a following for presentation as well as taste.

The vinyl lounge side of the business gives it more atmosphere than a standard daytime café, with music playing a bigger role in the setting than at most breakfast spots. It draws a mix of locals and visitors exploring Sea Point's café strip along Regent Road. Trading daily from early morning into the afternoon, it suits a leisurely weekend brunch as well as a quicker weekday breakfast before work.

Jordan Footwear Factory Outlet is a footwear factory shop on Voortrekker Road in Goodwood, selling shoes for men, women and children under the Jordan name alongside other brands including Bolton, Barker and Watson. Running as a factory outlet rather than a standard retail shoe shop, stock is generally sold directly off the shop floor rather than held in a wide range of backroom sizes.

Monthly specials are a regular feature, giving regular shoppers a reason to check in rather than buying only when they need a specific pair. It is based on Voortrekker Road in Goodwood, within the busy retail strip that runs through the Goodwood and Parow area. The shop trades six days a week, including Saturday and Sunday, making it accessible for weekend shoe shopping.

Jumbo Clothing is a fashion retailer on Voortrekker Road in Bellville, part of a long-running South African clothing chain that has now been trading for fifty years. The Bellville store sells menswear, womenswear, and children's clothing and footwear, positioned at value prices rather than as a premium fashion label.

Being part of a chain with that length of history gives the Bellville branch access to the group's buying scale and regular promotional ranges, while still functioning as a standard high-street clothing store for day-to-day shopping. It trades from Voortrekker Road, serving shoppers across Bellville and the surrounding Northern Suburbs. The store is a practical option for families buying everyday clothing and footwear across age groups in a single visit, rather than shopping separately for adults and children.

Just Skin Aesthetic Clinic is an aesthetic skincare clinic in Green Point offering facials, chemical peels, microdermabrasion and laser hair removal alongside other results-driven skin treatments. The clinic is registered as a private healthcare provider rather than a beauty salon, reflecting a more clinical approach to the treatments it offers.

Based on the first floor above Main Road and Upper Portswood Road, the clinic sits within the Portside Shopping Centre precinct in Green Point, convenient for clients combining a treatment with other errands in the area. It serves clients across Green Point, Sea Point and the City Bowl looking for targeted skin treatments rather than a general spa day. The clinic is closed over weekends, trading strictly on weekdays for scheduled appointments.

Kalk Bay Trading Post is an antiques and collectables shop on Main Road, next to Kalk Bay railway station. The stock runs through vintage furniture, old coins, maps and other retro memorabilia, the kind of browsing stock that rewards a slow look around rather than a quick in-and-out visit.

It trades alongside Kalk Bay's well-known run of bric-a-brac shops, vintage bookstores and art galleries, making it a natural stop for visitors already walking the strip rather than a destination on its own. The shop serves both local collectors and tourists passing through on a day out in Kalk Bay. It is open seven days a week, including weekend mornings, which suits the area's weekend foot traffic as much as weekday browsing.

Kalky's is a fish and chips shack at Kalk Bay Harbour that has been trading since 1986, built right at the water's edge where the local fishing fleet lands its catch. Fish is sourced from boats working out of the harbour rather than a supplier several steps removed from the water, so the catch on offer can change with what came in that day.

Seating is simple and harbourside rather than a sit-down restaurant setting, in keeping with its shack origins, and payment is cash only rather than by card. Having traded for close to forty years, it has become one of Kalk Bay's known landmarks for visitors touring the harbour. It stays open daily from mid-morning into the evening, making it workable for a late lunch or early dinner by the water.

Kauai at Constantia Village is a healthy-eating café serving wraps, salad bowls, smoothies, raw juices and barista-brewed coffee, with an all-day breakfast menu running alongside the main food range. Vegetarian and vegan options are available across most of the menu rather than limited to a single dish.

Orders can be placed in person, through the brand's own ordering app, or via delivery partners, giving customers more ways to get food than a typical in-store-only café. Trading from Constantia Village shopping centre, it serves shoppers and residents across Constantia and the Southern Suburbs looking for a lighter meal. It is open daily from early morning into the early evening, with a slightly shorter day on Sundays.

Kenridge Primary School is a public primary school in Kenridge, Durbanville, founded in 1955 and run today around stated values of kindness, perseverance and service. It offers the standard primary curriculum through to Grade 7, with its own extra-curricular programme covering sport, culture and other activities outside the classroom.

The school acts as a feeder for Durbanville High School and Fairmont High School, so most learners move on to one of those two high schools once they finish primary level. It maintains its own uniform and second-hand uniform exchange, along with published term schedules and a governing body structure typical of a public school. Classes run from morning until early afternoon, Monday to Friday, with a shorter day on Fridays, in line with the rest of the Durbanville school calendar.

Khoisan Gourmet produces and exports rooibos, honeybush and other indigenous South African herbal teas, along with Bourbon vanilla, from its facility in Ysterplaat. Rather than growing the raw product itself, the business focuses on processing, packing and getting these specialty lines to both local and international customers.

It operates as part of Libstar, a JSE-listed food and consumer goods group with a portfolio of manufacturing and processing businesses across South Africa, giving Khoisan Gourmet the backing and distribution reach of a listed group rather than operating as a small independent processor. The Ysterplaat site serves as both a production and export base for the business. It is a business-to-business operation rather than a shopfront, supplying retailers and export customers rather than selling directly to passing trade.

Kirstenhof Car Sales is a used-car dealership at the corner of Main and Aberfeldy Roads in Kirstenhof, trading since 2001. As an independent dealer rather than a franchised new-car showroom, the business sources and sells a changing stock of pre-owned vehicles rather than a fixed model range.

Customer service built around personal attention rather than high-volume sales has been a consistent part of how the dealership is known locally, with buyers dealt with directly rather than through a large sales floor team. Having operated from the same Kirstenhof corner for more than two decades, it has become a familiar stop for used-car buyers in the area. It serves Kirstenhof, Lakeside and the wider Deep South, trading six days a week and closed on Sundays.

Knead Bakery & Cafe's Kenilworth branch operates inside the Pick n Pay at the Pam Golding on Main development, on the corner of Summerley and Main Road. The bakery turns out fresh bread and pastries daily, served alongside brewed coffee for customers wanting to sit down rather than grab and go.

Trading from inside an established supermarket rather than a standalone shopfront means customers can combine a coffee stop with their regular grocery run. As part of the wider Knead bakery group, the branch benefits from recipes and baking standards shared across its other Cape Town locations. It serves shoppers and residents across Kenilworth and the surrounding Southern Suburbs, open daily with a later start on weekends than during the week.

Kommetjie Village Vet is a veterinary practice in Kommetjie forming part of the Two Oceans Veterinary Group, which operates several practices across the Cape Peninsula. The clinic covers routine wellness check-ups, vaccinations, dental care and general consultations, alongside diagnostics and surgical procedures for more serious cases.

Being part of a larger veterinary group gives the practice access to shared resources and referral support beyond what a single standalone vet could offer on its own, while still operating as the local, familiar practice for day-to-day pet care in the area. Emergency treatment is also available for urgent cases. It is based at Kommetjie On Main on Main Road, serving pet owners across Kommetjie and the surrounding Deep South peninsula communities, open weekdays and Saturday mornings.

KWIKSPAR Stellenberg is a branch of the SPAR convenience supermarket chain, which began in South Africa in 1963 when a group of independent wholesalers formed a network to supply local stores, and now numbers more than 2,500 independently owned outlets across the country. The Stellenberg branch runs its own in-store bakery and butchery alongside the standard grocery range.

As with other SPAR stores, it stocks the group's own-brand product range, backed by a money-back quality guarantee on SPAR-branded items, giving shoppers a value option alongside name-brand groceries. Being independently owned within the SPAR network means the store is run by its own local operator rather than head office directly. It trades from the Stellenberg Spar Centre on Haarlem Street, serving the Stellenberg and wider Bellville community, open daily including evenings.

La Perla is a long-established Mediterranean and seafood restaurant on the promenade corner of Church and Beach Roads in Sea Point, trading since 1957 and known locally as one of Cape Town's oldest surviving restaurants. The kitchen has built its reputation on seafood and Mediterranean dishes served in a traditional dining room rather than a casual bistro setting.

Takeaways are also available for customers who want the food without the formal sit-down service. Having operated from the same Sea Point corner for close to seventy years, it has outlasted most of the newer restaurants that have opened and closed along the same strip. It serves diners across Sea Point and visitors drawn specifically to its history, open daily from mid-morning into the evening for lunch and dinner service.

Look Its Me Hair Design is a hair salon on Korfbal Street in Beacon Valley, Mitchells Plain, offering a broad range of hair services including braiding, colouring, extensions and highlights. Chemical treatments such as keratin smoothing and permanent straightening are also available for clients managing curly or textured hair.

Children's haircuts are catered for alongside the main women's hair services, making it a workable option for parents booking for the whole family in one visit rather than finding a separate children's hair stylist. It is based on Korfbal Street in Beacon Valley, serving clients across Mitchells Plain and the surrounding suburbs. The range of chemical and styling services on offer suits clients after a specific look rather than a quick, basic trim.

Lotus River Community Health Centre is a public health facility on the corner of Delia and Anita Roads in Lotus River, providing general clinic services to the surrounding community. A dental clinic operates alongside the general health services, giving patients access to basic dental care without needing a separate referral to a private practice.

As a public facility rather than a private clinic, services are generally available at no or low cost to patients who qualify, making it an accessible option for residents who might otherwise go without routine care. It serves Lotus River and neighbouring Cape Flats suburbs including Ottery and Lansdowne. The centre operates during standard weekday working hours, in line with other public clinics run by the Western Cape health department.

Maggie's Cafe is a dog-friendly cafe and bar in Green Point that opened in February 2016, serving all-day café-style food with a cheffy twist rather than standard café fare. The kitchen has built a menu around dishes like breakfast poke bowls and egg-and-kimchi tacos, alongside more familiar café staples.

An extensive wine list runs alongside the food menu, giving the venue more of a bar feel in the evenings than a typical daytime café. Dogs are welcome on the premises, which has made it a particular draw for pet owners in the area who want to bring their dog along rather than leave it at home. It serves the Green Point and Sea Point area, open most days with a later start and earlier close on Sundays, and closed on Mondays.

Maphindi's Braai Place is a shisa nyama and butchery in Nyanga, grilling meat over an open flame for customers to eat on site rather than only selling raw cuts to take home. Alongside the grilled meat, the kitchen also serves magwinya, the fried dough also known as vetkoek, as a simpler alternative to a full braai plate.

Outdoor seating and a television for watching sport give it a social, communal atmosphere typical of a township shisa nyama, making it as much a gathering spot as a place to eat. It works well for groups and family-style sharing rather than individual plated meals. It is based on 3rd Avenue in Nyanga, serving the local community and visitors curious about the shisa nyama tradition, open daily into the early evening.

Markham is the largest standalone menswear retail chain in Southern Africa, with more than 325 stores across the region, and its Gugulethu Square branch stocks on-trend menswear, footwear, accessories and gadgets. Being part of a chain at that scale means frequent new stock drops and seasonal ranges rather than a slower-moving independent menswear shop.

The gadgets and accessories side of the range extends beyond clothing into items like headphones and other lifestyle tech, giving the store a broader draw than footwear and clothing alone. It trades from Shop 64 in Gugulethu Square, on the corner of NY1 and NY3, serving shoppers across Gugulethu and the surrounding Cape Flats suburbs. It is open seven days a week, with a shorter trading day on Sundays, fitting around weekday work and weekend shopping trips alike.

Markham's Vangate Mall branch in Athlone is part of Markham, the largest standalone menswear retail chain in Southern Africa with more than 325 stores nationwide. The store stocks on-trend menswear, footwear and accessories, along with gadgets and lifestyle tech items that go beyond a typical clothing range.

Trading inside Vangate Mall puts the store alongside the mall's other retailers and food outlets, making it an easy stop as part of a wider shopping trip rather than a standalone destination. Stock turns over regularly in line with the brand's seasonal ranges, which suits shoppers after current styles rather than basics only. It serves Athlone and the surrounding Vanguard Drive corridor, open daily into the evening on weekdays and Saturdays, with a slightly shorter day on Sundays.

Matroosfontein Primary School is a public primary school on Yorkweg in Matroosfontein, teaching around 500 learners under a staff of about 20 teachers. As a Quintile 4 school, it charges tuition fees to cover running costs, while still receiving a government subsidy per learner toward its operating budget.

Admission follows the standard process set out under the South African Schools Act, with parents required to submit documents such as birth certificates and immunisation records when registering a child, and registration for the following year typically opening around April. The school also has its own uniform policy that families are expected to follow. It serves families across Matroosfontein and the neighbouring Cape Town suburbs, operating on the standard public school calendar and weekday timetable.

Maya's Hardware is a hardware store in Thembokwezi Square in Mandalay, Khayelitsha, stocking building materials, LPG gas, DIY tools and a full range of paint, plumbing, electrical and garden supplies. Running from a single site within the mall, it covers most of what a household or small building job would need without having to visit several separate specialist shops.

Seasonal promotions, including paint deals around events like Black Friday, are a regular part of how the store markets to its local customer base. It serves residents across Khayelitsha, with Mandalay and the surrounding suburbs making up its core trade. The store keeps weekend hours as well as a full weekday schedule, open daily including Saturdays and Sundays, which suits shoppers tackling home projects outside the working week.

McDonald's Parklands is a branch of the McDonald's fast-food chain, trading from Parklands Junction Shopping Centre with a dedicated drive-thru lane alongside regular counter service. Self-service ordering kiosks are available inside for customers who prefer not to queue at the till, serving the chain's full standard menu.

Reviewers have pointed to the branch's consistency and quick-moving drive-thru as a reason to choose it over other fast-food options nearby, along with a modern, clean dining area for anyone eating in. Being part of a large international franchise means the same menu and recipes as any other McDonald's, run locally by the Parklands store's own staff. It serves the Parklands and Table View area, open long hours daily to cover breakfast through to late-night meals.
